<!-- name: Lava Lamp -->
<!-- board: a lava lamp that is your battery | big text on every 3.5" screen | the Freenove S3 3.5" (BETA) | pets hop instead of teleporting | POCKET MODE -->
**Lava Lamp.** Squachy has never once known how much battery he had left. He'd just keep talking until the screen went black mid-sentence, like a guy who refuses to check his gas gauge. That ends today. On the boards that carry a battery, there's now a little vaporwave **lava lamp** tucked under the menu button, and the lava is your charge. Blobs drift up and sink back. The lava wanders from pink to purple to cyan. It is, objectively, the most relaxing fuel gauge ever built.

<p align="center"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skizzophrenic/SquachWatch-CYD/v1.34.0/docs/lava-lamp.gif" width="480" alt="On the 3.5 inch screen, a small lava lamp with a purple cap sits under the menu button, half full of glowing lava with blobs drifting in it, while Squachy stands in a night forest. Plugged in, bubbles race up through the lava and the cap and base scroll through the rainbow. Nearly flat, the lamp holds a thin layer of lava that flickers. The SquachMesh warning opens as a big Windows 95 window titled THIS MAKES YOU TRACKABLE, and the alert screen shows IGNORE in bold. A unicorn-horned visitor named YETI stands beside Squachy at the new, bigger size. Squachy walks to the right edge and C1iPPY the paperclip hops across in front of him to his other side. Last, C1iPPY is thrown, lands, and says Attached to nothing now. Thanks for that. in a small bold balloon."></p>

**The lamp.** Plug in and the lamp knows: bubbles stream up through the lava, the glow around the glass beats like a heart, and a rainbow scrolls through the cap and base. Unplug and it settles back to purple. Under 10% it flickers like a bulb on its last legs, which is your cue. Full, it twinkles. On the T-Watch it reads the power chip, so it's exact. On the Freenove S3 boards there's no charging wire to read, so the lamp watches the battery's voltage instead: plugging in makes it jump, and it notices within a few seconds. Boards with no battery don't get a lamp at all, and look exactly as they did. On the 3.5" it's drawn three times the size, because a lava lamp you have to squint at is just sad.

**Big text on the 3.5".** Every 480x320 screen got its glasses back. About thirty screens use a bigger, rounder font now, the buttons are taller, and the SquachMesh warning and the phrase screens open as proper Windows 95 windows, title bar and all. MORE INFO pages through its text in big type instead of cramming. Squachy got resized too, screen by screen, picked off sliders of real emulator pictures: much bigger on the 3.5" in both orientations, and bigger with company on everything else, so a visitor or a crowd doesn't shrink everybody to ants. In portrait on the 3.5", Squachy and a visitor now stand together in the middle of the screen instead of huddling at the bottom like they're waiting for a bus. He also no longer floats off the floor at his LARGE size. He was never meant to fly. Not like that.

**The Freenove ESP32-S3 3.5" (BETA).** The black one, FNK0104N: a 320x480 panel on a four-lane QSPI bus that the usual display library can't drive, so it got its own driver, at 23-40 fps. Pets come out at double size there, and their speech balloons stay small and bold so C1iPPY's advice doesn't cover half the screen. It's on the flasher as a BETA. Its little sibling, the Freenove S3 2.8", went from 19 to 40 fps: the screen now goes out by DMA in a task of its own, at 80 MHz.

**No more teleporting pets.** When Squachy wandered close to the edge, C1iPPY and T0@$TY used to blink out of existence and reappear on his other side, like a cheap magic trick. Now they hop across, and the further they have to go, the bigger the hop. The iron ball rolls after him when he's been carried off. And if you pick Squachy up while the lil guy or the yeti is visiting, they walk off in a huff instead of vanishing into thin air.

**POCKET MODE.** Turn the screen off with the BOOT button (the crown on the watch) and now only another press wakes it. A touch won't, so a board in a pocket or a bag can't be woken by your keys. Alerts still light it for their card and then it goes dark again, and the very first time, a note tells you how to get back out. While we were in there: an alert used to leave a button-darkened screen on for its whole timeout, which felt like the button had been undone. It doesn't anymore.

**SEEN AT.** A board with a GPS fix now keeps each catch with where it was. Long-press a device in the LOG and it shows SEEN AT and the spot, for anything the log ever kept with a position.

### The actually-useful part

**Added**
- A lava-lamp battery gauge under the menu button on the Freenove S3 2.8" and 3.5" and the T-Watch S3: filled to the charge, bubbles and a rainbow cap on the cable, a flicker under 10%, a twinkle when full. Triple size on the 3.5". Boards with no battery show nothing.
- The Freenove ESP32-S3 3.5" (FNK0104N) as a BETA on the flasher: its own QSPI driver, touch, SD, LED and battery pins, pets at double size.
- POCKET MODE: with the screen turned off by BOOT or the crown, only another press turns it back on. A one-time note says how.
- SEEN AT on a LOG long-press for any device kept with a GPS position.
- Console `BATT` on the Freenove S3 boards prints the lamp's last three minutes of readings.
- Emulator: `SQUACHSIM_BATT=54` (or `54c` on the cable), `SQUACHSIM_WANDER`, `SQUACHSIM_WANDERAT` and `SQUACHSIM_PETLOG`.

**Changed**
- Every 480x320 screen: a bigger body font on about thirty screens, taller buttons, Windows 95 windows for the SquachMesh warning and phrase screens, and MORE INFO in big type with paging.
- Squachy's size picked per screen for every panel, alone, with a visitor and in a crowd. A visit on the 3.5" in portrait stands in the middle. The StickS3 and Cardputer keep one row of counter tiles, count only.
- Pets hop to a spot that jumps instead of appearing there, the ball rolls, and the lil guy and the yeti walk off when Squachy is picked up.
- Pet balloons on the 3.5" are drawn at the screen's own size, in the medium font, in bold.
- IGNORE (and MUTED) on the alert is bold.
- Freenove S3 2.8": the frame goes out by DMA in its own task at 80 MHz, 19 to 40 fps.
- A rewritten FAQ, and a README, DETECTIONS, BUILD and LORA brought up to date.

**Fixed**
- Squachy floated above the floor at the LARGE size.
- An alert left a screen the button had turned off lit for the whole timeout.
